long_biography.plain_text:
Working with Henadiy Boholiubov, Ihor Kolomoiskyi founded PrivatBank during Ukraine's early private-banking era and used the wider Privat Group to expand into oil, ferroalloys, aviation and media. The combination of a large retail bank and industrial holdings made banking and investment the durable engine of his fortune.

The portfolio has since changed substantially. Ukraine took PrivatBank into state ownership in 2016, and shares in Ukrnafta and Ukrtatnafta were transferred to the state in 2022, removing three widely cited assets from his current ownership. One continuing disclosed interest is 1+1 media. The group identifies Kolomoiskyi as its ultimate beneficial owner while noting that corporate-rights management was delegated to its chief executive for five years.

uncertainties: Ihor Kolomoiskyi is adopted as the preferred Ukrainian-derived English form because the National Bank of Ukraine uses it. Igor Kolomoyskyi is the input form; Forbes uses Ihor Kolomoyskyy, Reuters uses Ihor Kolomoiskiy, and the existing canonical profile uses Ihor Kolomoyskyi. These are transliteration variants, not identity conflicts.

Valeriyovych is used for the patronymic because Reuters supplies that English form and the Ukrainian university record gives Валерійович. Alternative romanizations include Valeriiovych and Valeryevich.

Ukrnafta and Ukrtatnafta are treated as former private interests because their shares were forcibly transferred into state property in 2022. The governing framework allows later return or compensation, so the biographies do not claim permanent extinguishment beyond the present state-ownership position.
